🌍 Iranian art and cinema draw praise at World Culture Festival in Karachi

📌 Islamabad, IRNA — Iranian artworks and films have received a warm reception at the 2026 World Culture Festival in Pakistan’s port city of Karachi, where artists from around the world have gathered to showcase their work and promote cultural exchange.

Iran took part in the international event with a delegation of artists specializing in painting, calligraphy, and cinema, invited by the Karachi Arts Council.
​
Iranian artworks attracted particular attention for their techniques, themes, and distinctive cultural identity.
​
One of the festival’s main attractions is an international visual arts exhibition titled “The Canvas of Peace,” which brings together works by local and international artists to celebrate cultural diversity and encourage artistic cooperation and intercultural dialogue.
​
The festival also features the screening of an Iranian short film, “Cradle of Silence,” directed by Mostafa Mehraban. The drama explores grief, loss, family relationships, and difficult life choices.
​
The World Culture Festival concludes on Sunday, November 22. It began on October 29, bringing together artists, creators, and producers from around the world to share their cultures and co-create art.
​
According to the Arts Council of Pakistan Karachi, more than 1,000 artists from at least 150 countries attended the festival.
